issues.legal_issue: A revenue officer cannot use a general review power concerning compensation decisions to reopen a final determination of occupancy-tenancy status and rent.
material_facts: A Deputy Commissioner determined under the land-reform scheme that the proprietor held the disputed lands as an occupancy tenant and settled the rent payable.
No appeal was brought against that determination, which became final.
A Nistar Officer later initiated proceedings to reopen the determination and, for another set of lands, made an order reviewing the earlier determination.
issues.conclusion: The Nistar Officer had no jurisdiction to reopen or review the final determination because the review power applied to decisions under the compensation provision, not to determinations of occupancy-tenancy status and rent.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 13 and 15(3) of the Madhya Pradesh Abolition of Proprietary Rights (Estates, Mahals, Alienated Lands) Act, the specified authorities could review orders made under section 13 concerning compensation and the land vesting in the State. Those provisions did not apply to a Deputy Commissioner's determination under section 40 concerning occupancy-tenancy status and rent. Section 84 provided an appeal from a revenue decision, but the Act provided no power to review the section 40 determination; it therefore became final when not appealed.

predicates.land_reform_reopening_proceeding: A revenue officer conducts a proceeding to reopen a determination made under a land-reform scheme.
predicates.prior_occupancy_and_rent_determination_f: An earlier determination established occupancy-tenancy status and rent, and it became final without being overturned on appeal.
predicates.review_authority_did_not_cover_that_dete: The available review authority did not extend to the kind of determination the officer sought to reopen.

issues.definition: When a revenue officer seeks to reopen a final determination of occupancy-tenancy status and rent in a land-reform proceeding, and the available review authority does not cover that determination, the reopening is without jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: The power to prepare annual revenue papers does not authorize correction of an earlier year's entries merely because they are alleged to have been mistaken.
material_facts: Earlier annual papers repeatedly recorded the disputed lands as occupancy-tenancy holdings of the respondents.
The Nistar Officer relied on a later inspection to describe entries as mistakes, to question the transfers, and to alter the records concerning cultivation.
The record alterations were intended to reopen a matter already determined under the land-reform scheme.
issues.conclusion: The annual-papers provision did not authorize correction of earlier entries on the ground of mistake, and the Nistar Officer had no jurisdiction to make the corrections to reopen the matter already decided.
issues.legal_principle: Section 47(1) of the Central Provinces Land Revenue Act, 1917, authorized preparation of annual papers recording subsequent changes in the relevant records; it did not provide for investigating and correcting the correctness of entries made in earlier years. Section 46 specified grounds for modifying entries in the record of rights, and an alleged mistake about earlier cultivation was not among the grounds identified by the Court. The Court approved Mangloo v. Board of Revenue, I.L.R. 1954 Nag. 143, on the limited scope of section 47(1).

predicates.annual_revenue_record_proceeding: An officer acts in a proceeding concerning preparation or correction of annual revenue records.
predicates.correction_targets_prior_year_error: The officer seeks to alter an entry from an earlier year because it is alleged to have been mistaken when made.
predicates.alleged_error_is_not_a_later_change: The asserted basis for correction is not a change that occurred after the earlier entry was made.

issues.definition: In an annual revenue-record proceeding, a prior entry cannot be corrected under the annual-record power when the asserted basis is an alleged original error rather than a later change.
